cited_by.label: Saul and the witch of Endor
8A.20 Those in government are not to consult mediums or spiritists for guidance but are to inquire of the LORD.

precepts.text: Israel is forbidden to use divination, enchantment, or to consult with familiar spirits.
precepts.point: The last straw for Saul was seeking that familiar spirit. Through Samuel the Most High told him he would join him the next day. The difference is that Samuel died righteously.
precepts.why:
The law is plain: “There shall not be found among you any one” that “useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch”, nor “a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer.” Israel is forbidden to use divination, enchantment, or to consult with familiar spirits.

Saul died “for his transgression which he committed against the Lord, even against the word of the Lord, which he kept not, and also for asking counsel of one that had a familiar spirit, to enquire of it”. That was the last straw for him. The left hand of the Most High is real, and people who meddle with it get entangled and get spirits put on them. It is not our custom.

precepts.text: Suffer not a witch to live; such practices are not Israel's custom.
precepts.point: The last straw for Saul was seeking that familiar spirit. Through Samuel the Most High told him he would join him the next day. The difference is that Samuel died righteously.
precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not suffer a witch to live.” Witchcraft and consulting familiar spirits are not Israel's custom. The law does not even suffer the witch to live among the people.

That is what Saul turned to. The king who should have kept the word of the Lord went seeking counsel from a woman that the law says not to suffer to live, and he “enquired not of the Lord: therefore he slew him, and turned the kingdom unto David the son of Jesse.”

precepts.text: Saul sought out a woman with a familiar spirit at Endor and disguised himself to go to her by night.
precepts.point: The last straw for Saul was seeking that familiar spirit. Through Samuel the Most High told him he would join him the next day. The difference is that Samuel died righteously.
precepts.why:
Here is the very thing Chronicles speaks of. Saul told his servants, “Seek me a woman that hath a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and enquire of her.” They found one at Endor, and “Saul disguised himself, and put on other raiment,” and came to her by night with two men.

He asked her, “divine unto me by the familiar spirit, and bring me him up, whom I shall name unto thee.” The one he wanted brought up was Samuel. This is Saul “asking counsel of one that had a familiar spirit, to enquire of it”, the last straw that cost him his life and his kingdom.

precepts.text: Saul was afraid of the Philistine host and inquired of the Most High, who answered him not by dreams, Urim, or prophets, so he turned to the witch.
precepts.point: The last straw for Saul was seeking that familiar spirit. Through Samuel the Most High told him he would join him the next day. The difference is that Samuel died righteously.
precepts.why:
This is what drove Saul to the witch. “And when Saul saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.” He enquired of the Most High, “the Lord answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.”

So Saul turned to the witch instead. Rather than inquiring of the Most High, he went to the left hand, and that is why Chronicles records that he “enquired not of the Lord: therefore he slew him”.

precepts.text: The woman brought up Samuel, an old man covered with a mantle, and Saul bowed himself to the ground before the word she carried.
precepts.point: The last straw for Saul was seeking that familiar spirit. Through Samuel the Most High told him he would join him the next day. The difference is that Samuel died righteously.
precepts.why:
The woman brought up Samuel. “And when the woman saw Samuel, she cried with a loud voice”, and she knew then who had come to her: “Why hast thou deceived me? for thou art Saul.” She said, “I saw gods ascending out of the earth”, and “An old man cometh up; and he is covered with a mantle.” Saul “perceived that it was Samuel, and he stooped with his face to the ground, and bowed himself.”

Through Samuel the Most High told Saul he would join him the next day. Both men died, but the difference is that Samuel died righteously. Saul died for his transgression, for not keeping the word of the Lord, and for seeking that familiar spirit.

precepts.text: Israel rejected the Most High as king and demanded a king like the other nations, which is how Saul came to reign.
precepts.point: The last straw for Saul was seeking that familiar spirit. Through Samuel the Most High told him he would join him the next day. The difference is that Samuel died righteously.
precepts.why:
This is how Saul came to reign at all. Israel came to Samuel and said, “make us a king to judge us like all the nations.” “But the thing displeased Samuel”, and he prayed. The Most High answered, “they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them.”

Israel rejected the Most High as their king and demanded a king like the other nations, and Saul was that king. He ended by keeping not the word of the Lord and asking counsel of a familiar spirit, so the Most High slew him and “turned the kingdom unto David the son of Jesse.”

points: The Philistines fought Israel, the men of Israel fled and fell slain in mount Gilboa, and the Philistines killed Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua, the sons of Saul.

The battle went hard against Saul, the archers wounded him, and he asked his armourbearer to run him through so the uncircumcised would not abuse him. The armourbearer was too afraid, so Saul fell on his own sword and died.
Saul died, his three sons, and all his house together, and when Israel saw it they forsook their cities and fled, and the Philistines came and dwelt in them.

The next day the Philistines came to strip the slain, found Saul and his sons fallen in Gilboa, took his head and his armour, and sent word throughout their land to carry tidings to their idols and to the people.

They put his armour in the house of their gods and fastened his head in the temple of Dagon. Dagon was the fish god, and its likeness is carried over into false religion in the fish-shaped mitre and the fish symbol.

When Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul, all their valiant men arose, took the bodies of Saul and his sons, brought them to Jabesh, buried their bones under the oak, and fasted seven days.

Saul died for his transgression against the Most High, for not keeping His word, and for asking counsel of one that had a familiar spirit rather than inquiring of the Most High. Therefore the Most High slew him and turned the kingdom to David the son of Jesse.

Saul had gone to a woman with a familiar spirit to bring up Samuel. The left hand of the Most High is real. People who meddle with that get entangled and get spirits put on them. It is not our custom.
The last straw for Saul was seeking that familiar spirit. Through Samuel the Most High told him he would join him the next day. The difference is that Samuel died righteously.
